verifications.note: "Northern Border Pipeline is a medium-sized 1,412-mile pipeline running from the Montana-Saskatchewan border near Port of Morgan, Montana, to Fort Hayden, Indiana." — states both endpoints verbatim as recorded (StartLocation/StartState, EndLocation/EndState).

FERC order text, p.355: "...granted Northern Border a permit authorizing Northern Border to construct, operate, maintain and connect natural gas transmission facilities at the international boundary near Port of Morgan, Montana." — corroborates the start point independently of Rextag.

Page description metadata: "The 2,272km-long Northern Border gas pipeline is operated by TC Energy... starts at Montana (the US) and ends in Indiana (the US)." — third independent source, corroborates both endpoint states (fetched via Wayback capture 20240220215225 after a live 403; page content unchanged from that snapshot per url_verifier's live 200 check).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded StartLocation/StartState/Province (Port of Morgan, Montana) and EndLocation/EndState/Province (Fort Hayden, Indiana) are directly and verbatim corroborated by Rextag, with the Montana border-crossing point independently corroborated by a 1982 FERC certificate order (eba-net.org) and both endpoint states (Montana -> Indiana) independently corroborated by offshore-technology.com. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: the recorded StartCountryOrArea is 'Canada', but Montana is a U.S. state and every source describing this crossing (Rextag, the FERC order, TC Energy's own site, offshore-technology.com) treats Port of Morgan/Morgan, Montana as the U.S. side of the Montana-Saskatchewan border, i.e. United States, not Canada -- offshore-technology.com states explicitly the pipeline 'starts at Montana (the US)'. StartCountryOrArea='Canada' appears to be a data error (should be United States, or the row's true start point should be re-pointed to the Canadian side, e.g. Saskatchewan, with StartLocation/StartState/Province corrected to match). Not corrected here per the recovery contract's 'emit the SAME value' rule; flagging for the orchestrator to route to Update. No source names 'Fort Hayden, Indiana' more granularly than the two given here (Wikipedia and the TC Energy/pipelineawareness.org/ND Legislative Council documents describe the eastern terminus only generically as 'the Chicago market area' / 'Chicago', and a 1980s FERC ANGTA history document names the original ANGTS eastern-leg proposal's terminus as 'Dwight, Illinois' -- an earlier planning-stage endpoint, not necessarily the built pipeline's current interconnect); Rextag and offshore-technology.com remain the only two sources found naming Indiana specifically for the current end point, both independent of each other and of the sheet.
